answers.explanation: MIME works inside the message. SMTP still carries text; MIME labels and encodes the content so it fits.
multipart/mixed: several parts of different types, split by a boundary.
Alternative parts are the same content in different forms.
Base64. It's the usual Content-Transfer-Encoding for attachments.
The sender writes that label. It can say anything.
Each part starts with --boundary, and the last one is --boundary--.
